information.description:
A rising star in MAX-TAC’s ranks that was recruited after her own cyberpsychotic outburst, Melissa has quickly become a Lieutenant of a SPAR team. She has already earned a rather bloodthirsty reputation, even among her other cyberware-laden peers. Melissa will not hesitate to dice a target into small chunks, laugh while doing so, and then do an interview a bout how she’s helping to save the city. All of which she does with extreme proficiency, as she’s got some of the best (and most) combat cyberware of any MAX-TAC member.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Max-Tac).

Threat level: Elite Hardened Boss

description.value: Experts in combat who use their fighting prowess to dominate in the lawless time of the Red.
Throwing hands, does ignore half armor.

The preferred pistol among Night City cops – light, wieldy, and easy on the recoil, it's perfect for taking down enemies without necessarily killing them on the spot. Thanks to its relatively small dimensions, the gun has also found a loyal following among those who prefer a concealed carry: the Lexington easily fits in a coat pocket or purse. And for design lovers, its classic 2030s frame remains stunning as ever.

Cost: 750eb (Expensive)

Class: Heavy Pistol • Skill: Handgun • Range: Pistol

Damage: 3d6 • Capacity: 21 • ROF: 2 • Hands: 1

Alt. Firing Modes: Autofire (Machine Pistol 3), Suppressive Fire

Concealable: Yes

Slots: 2 • Attachments: Pistol Autosear, Power Rebuild • Mods: None

Special Features: None.

Range: Pistol
Pre-installed: Pistol Autosear, Power Rebuild (effects already included in these stats)
Alt. fire: Autofire (Machine Pistol 3), Suppressive Fire

Foundry notes:

  • Its range tables come from this module's DV Tables compendium; run the module's "Use Corgo's 77 DV Tables" macro once per world (see the module README).

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Weapons > Weapon Catalog).

Cost: 500eb (Expensive) ♦ Required Slots: 1

Fits: All Ranged Weapons capable of Autofire that expend 10 rounds when using Autofire, except Machine Guns

By optimizing fire rate, ammo conservation becomes easy. Crucial for mercs on long-term assignments or punks with 6eb in their pocket.

The weapon now only expends 6 rounds when using Autofire.

NOTE: Credit to the Cyberpunk RUSH LC for the inspiration behind this item.

Attachment slots: 1

Cost: 10,000eb (Super Luxury)

Built for MAX-TAC, this helmet contains the most robust optical suite ever packed into headgear. A fully kitted-out model can locate and track threats in any environment, while its nano-alloy easily resists small arms fire without over-encumbering its user. To put it simply, the Max-Helm’s capabilities are as insane as its users are.

SP 16 Head Armor with an Armor Penalty of -1 to REF, and -2 to DEX and MOVE. All ablation this armor would suffer is reduced by 1 (Minimum 0). This armor’s SP is not halved by Martial Arts Attacks and Special Moves. Has built-in Smart Ears (w/ Level Damper and Radio Communicator) and modified Smart Glasses with 8 Option Slots for Cybereye Options. This armor is also capable of installing Subdermal Armor Cyberware Enhancements. This armor repairs itself for 1 point of lost SP at the end of each day in which it does not lose SP.

Covers: Head
SP: 16
Armor Penalty: -1 REF, -2 DEX, -2 MOVE

Foundry notes:

  • Corgo's penalty is -1 REF, -2 DEX, -2 MOVE. The sheet applies one penalty to all three stats, so it uses -2; add the difference back by hand for the lighter stat(s).

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Armor & Fashion > Armor Catalog).

Cost: 500eb (Expensive)

“FUCK ARMOR PENALTIES.” — Anonymous Lizard

SP 16 or lower Body/Head Armor Enhancement. Cannot be installed in any form of Metalgear. All of the armor’s Armor Penalties (if any), are reduced by 1 (Minimum 0). Armor with this enhancement cannot be combined with a kit or tech upgraded to resemble any form of Fashion it does not already appear as by default. This enhancement cannot be Tech Upgraded to further reduce Armor Penalties.

Type: Armor Enhancement (Body/Head, SP 16 or lower, not Metalgear)
Attachment slots: 0

Foundry notes:

  • Armor Enhancement rules: one Enhancement per piece of armor (armor worn on both body and head counts as one piece); not for cyberware armor (Skinweave, Subdermal Armor) or armor that's part of an ACPA or vehicle; SP limits use the armor's fully repaired SP; a Tech installs or removes one in 1 hour with no check; they don't count as Tech Upgrades for Upgrade Expertise. Armor Attachments have no limit per armor unless stated.
  • All of the armor's Armor Penalties drop by 1 (minimum 0); lower its penalty by hand.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Armor & Fashion > Armor Enhancements & Kits).

Cost: 15,000eb (Super-Luxury)

Rolled out in 2069, this next-gen tactical armor uses flexible materials and crystalline gels for maximum protection at very little weight. Its glowing lines may resemble a fashion statement, but in reality, they’re part of a powered exoshell that can accept external cybernetics such as EMP buffers, dermal reinforcements, or even optical camouflage.

SP 16 Body Armor with an Armor Penalty of -1 to REF, and -2 to DEX and MOVE. All ablation this armor would suffer is reduced by 1 (Minimum 0). This armor’s SP is not halved by Martial Arts Attacks and Special Moves. Has 1 Option Slot for External Body Cyberware, which ignores installation requirements (including being an FBC and required Option Slots), but cannot install cyberware that grants or restores SP.

This armor is also capable of installing Subdermal Armor Cyberware Enhancements. While worn, the user may access any of the armor’s installed Cyberware, which does not cause any Humanity Loss or consume any of their Cyberware Option Slots. This armor repairs itself for 1 point of lost SP at the end of a day in which it does not lose SP.

A cybernetical replacement arm. Comes with a free hand.

Category: Luxury • Fabrication: DV29 - 5,000eb - 1 Month

Humanity Loss: 14 (4d6) • Install: Hospital

Discontinued in 2069 after a flood of reports detailing its poor interface with neural processors and prefrontal cortexes, these extremely rare arm implants are some of the best Mantis Blade models ever designed. The synth-muscles are faster, synaptic responses more intense, the bloodthirst more fervent, and lethality extremely evident.

Iconic Paired Cyberarm Options. Requires Paired Cyberarms and 2 Cyberarm Option Slots on each Cyberarm. Counts as 2 installations of Borgware. Each arm now has a One-Handed Excellent Quality Heavy Melee Weapon that can be successfully concealed without a Check and can be drawn and stowed without an Action. While the weapon is “popped up,” the user can’t hold anything in that arm’s hand. While both blades are “popped up,” the user can wield both blades as a single EQ ROF 2 Very Heavy Melee Weapon with a 4m/yds range and can negate the normal movement penalty for climbing.

Whenever either of these blades inflicts a Critical Injury, the user rolls three times on the Critical Injury table and chooses their favorite option for the victim to suffer. If the user has currently active Speedware and a total Initiative Bonus of +4 or higher, when rolling for damage with these blades, any damage die that land on a 1 are re-rolled until they result in a higher value.

Fabrication: DV29 - 5,000eb - 1 Month
Type: Cyberarm
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 2

Foundry notes:

  • Iconic: it can't be bought or sourced on the street, can't be fabricated without its Blueprint, can't be taken during Character Generation, and once acquired can't be destroyed unless the player agrees to it beforehand.
  • The price is the Luxury benchmark, for working out repairs and Tech Upgrades. Iconics can't be bought.
  • One item for the pair, as Corgo installs them together. Its size is the 2 slots it takes in one arm; it needs 2 in each.
  • Counts as two installations of Borgware for Maximum Humanity Loss, applied by hand.
  • Cyberware items have no Quality field, so the Excellent Quality is in the text only.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Becoming Iconic > Iconic Cyberware).
The arm and installed options are not affected by EMP effects.
